en: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us: Ibn Idris narrated to us; (and a different chain) Minjab ibn al-Harith at-Tamimi narrated to us: Ibn Mushir narrated to us; (and a different chain) Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and 'Ali ibn Khashram both narrated to us: 'Isa ibn Yunus reported to us; (and a different chain) Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, all of them from al-A'mash with this chain of narration, similar to it. Minjab added in his narration from Ibn Mushir: Al-A'mash said: And 'Amr ibn Murrah narrated to me from Shaqiq, from 'Abdullah, the like of it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki' and Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (and a different chain) Ibn Numayr narrated to us—and the wording is his: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, who said: We were sitting at the door of 'Abdullah waiting for him, when Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah an-Nakha'i passed by us, so we said: "Inform him of our presence." He entered upon him, and it was not long before 'Abdullah came out to us and said: "I was informed of your presence, but nothing prevents me from coming out to you except that I dislike causing you boredom. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, used to space out the days when admonishing us, out of fear that weariness might overtake us."

Harun ibn Ma'ruf and Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli both narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Abu Sakhr reported to me, from Ibn Qusayt, from 'Urwah ibn az-Zubayr, from 'A'ishah, who said: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, prayed, he would stand until his feet cracked. 'A'ishah said: "O Messenger of Allah, do you do this when Allah has already forgiven you what preceded of your sin and what came after?" He said: "O 'A'ishah, should I not be a grateful servant?"

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Numayr both narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn 'Ilaqah, who heard al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah say: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, stood in prayer until his feet swelled. They said: "Allah has already forgiven you what preceded of your sin and what came after." He said: "Should I not be a grateful servant?"

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn 'Ilaqah, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, prayed until his feet became swollen, so it was said to him: "Do you burden yourself with this when Allah has already forgiven you what preceded of your sin and what came after?" He said: "Should I not be a grateful servant?"

Hasan al-Hulwani narrated it to us: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn al-Muttalib narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah with this chain of narration, and he did not mention: "and receive glad tidings."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad reported to us: Musa ibn 'Uqbah reported to us; (and a different chain) Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me—and the wording is his: Bahz narrated to us: Wuheyb narrated to us: Musa ibn 'Uqbah narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn 'Awf narrate from 'A'ishah, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, that she used to say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Follow the right course, seek moderation, and receive glad tidings, for no one's deeds will ever admit him into Paradise." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even me, unless Allah encompasses me with mercy from Him. And know that the most beloved of deeds to Allah is that which is most consistent, even if it is small."

Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to me: Al-Hasan ibn A'yan narrated to us: Ma'qil narrated to us, from Abu az-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say: "The deeds of none among you will admit him into Paradise, nor will they save him from the Fire—nor me, except by mercy from Allah."
Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash with both chains of narration, like the narration of Ibn Numayr.
Ibn Numayr narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, the like of it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb both narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, the like of it, and he added: "and receive glad tidings."

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Seek moderation, follow the right course, and know that none among you will be saved by his deeds." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, not even you?" He said: "Not even me, unless Allah encompasses me with mercy from Him and grace."

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Abu 'Abbad Yahya ibn 'Abbad narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us: Ibn Shihab narrated to us, from Abu 'Ubayd, the freed slave of 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn 'Awf, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "The deeds of none of you will ever admit him into Paradise." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even me, unless Allah encompasses me with grace from Him and mercy."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "There is no one whose deeds will save him." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even me, unless Allah reaches me with mercy from Him."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Ibn 'Awn, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "There is no one among you whose deeds will save him." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even me, unless Allah encompasses me with forgiveness from Him and mercy." And Ibn 'Awn gestured with his hand like this, pointing over his head: "Not even me, unless Allah encompasses me with forgiveness from Him and mercy."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Hammad—meaning Ibn Zayd—narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "There is no one whose deeds will admit him into Paradise." It was said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even me, unless my Lord encompasses me with mercy."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Bukayr, from Busr ibn Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, that he said: "The deeds of none of you will ever save him." A man said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even me, unless Allah encompasses me with mercy from Him; but follow the right course." And Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la as-Sadafi narrated it to me: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb reported to us: 'Amr ibn al-Harith reported to me, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj with this chain of narration, except that he said: "with mercy from Him and grace," and did not mention: "but follow the right course."

Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli narrated to me: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Abu Sakhr reported to me, from Ibn Qusayt, that 'Urwah narrated to him that 'A'ishah, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, left her place at night. She said: I felt jealous about him. Then he came and saw what I was doing, so he said: "What is the matter with you, O 'A'ishah? Have you become jealous?" I said: "How could someone like me not feel jealous over someone like you?" The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Has your devil come to you?" She said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there a devil with me?" He said: "Yes." I said: "And with every human being?" He said: "Yes." I said: "And with you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes, but my Lord helped me against him until he submitted."

Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us: 'Abd ar-Rahman—meaning Ibn Mahdi—narrated to us, from Sufyan; (and a different chain) Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from 'Ammar ibn Ruzayq, both from Mansur with the chain of Jarir, the like of his hadith, except that in the hadith of Sufyan: "and there has been appointed over him his companion from among the jinn and his companion from among the angels."

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—Ishaq said: reported to us, while 'Uthman said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from his father, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "There is no one among you except that there has been assigned over him his companion from among the jinn." They said: "And you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "And me, except that Allah has helped me against him, so he has submitted, and he does not command me except with good."

Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to me: Al-Hasan ibn A'yan narrated to us: Ma'qil narrated to us, from Abu az-Zubayr, from Jabir, that he heard the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say: "Satan dispatches his raiding parties so that they tempt people into tribulation, and the one of them greatest in status with him is the one who causes the greatest tribulation."

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Kurayb's—they said: Abu Mu'awiyah reported to us: Al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Indeed, Iblis places his throne upon the water, then he sends out his detachments; the closest of them to him in status is the one greatest in causing tribulation. One of them comes and says: 'I did such-and-such,' so he says: 'You have done nothing.' He said: Then one of them comes and says: 'I did not leave him until I separated him from his wife.' He said: So he draws him close to himself and says: 'How excellent you are!'" Al-A'mash said: I believe he said: "and he embraces him."

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—Ishaq said: reported to us, while 'Uthman said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say: "Indeed, the throne of Iblis is upon the sea, and he sends out his raiding parties to tempt people, and the greatest of them in his sight is the one who causes the greatest tribulation."
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us: Waki' narrated to us; (and a different chain) Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, both from al-A'mash with this chain of narration.

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—Ishaq said: reported to us, while 'Uthman said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say: "Indeed, Satan has despaired of being worshipped by the worshipers in the Arabian Peninsula, but [he seeks] to incite discord between them."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us: 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and he said: "Tell me of a tree that is like—or resembles—the Muslim man: its leaves do not fall..." Ibrahim said: perhaps Muslim said: "and it yields its fruit." And thus I found it with other than me as well: "and it yields its fruit all the time." Ibn 'Umar said: It occurred to me that it is the date-palm, but I saw that Abu Bakr and 'Umar were not speaking, so I disliked speaking or saying anything. 'Umar said: "That you had said it would have been more beloved to me than such-and-such."

Ibn Numayr narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Sayf narrated to us, saying: I heard Mujahid say: I heard Ibn 'Umar say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was brought palm pith... and he mentioned the like of their hadith.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi 'Umar both narrated to us: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: I accompanied Ibn 'Umar to Madinah and did not hear him narrate from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, except a single hadith. He said: We were with the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, when palm pith was brought to him... and he mentioned similar to their hadith.

Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Ghubari narrated to me: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us: Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu al-Khalil ad-Duba'i, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said one day to his companions: "Tell me about a tree whose likeness is like the likeness of the believer." The people began mentioning trees of the desert. Ibn 'Umar said: It was cast into my mind—or it occurred to my heart—that it was the date-palm, so I wanted to say it, but then I noticed the elders of the people, so I felt too in awe to speak. When they remained silent, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "It is the date-palm."

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, and 'Ali ibn Hujr as-Sa'di narrated to us—and the wording is Yahya's—they said: Isma'il—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Dinar reported to me that he heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Indeed, among trees there is a tree whose leaves do not fall, and it is the likeness of the Muslim; so tell me what it is." The people's thoughts turned to the trees of the desert. 'Abdullah said: It occurred to my mind that it was the date-palm, but I was shy. Then they said: "Tell us what it is, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "It is the date-palm." He said: So I mentioned that to 'Umar, and he said: "That you had said 'it is the date-palm' would have been more beloved to me than such-and-such."
